where: Centre pad of the steering wheel
Some two-wheelers: a button on the left switch block

when.s: You approach a blind hairpin
when.d: A short honk warns oncoming traffic.

when.s: You're in a silence zone or the traffic is jammed
when.d: Don't honk - it achieves nothing and disturbs others.

ctrl_horn.mistake: Continuous honking at signals or behind slow vehicles.

ctrl_headlamp.more: The headlamp switch (often on the indicator stalk) turns on parking lights, low beam and - by pushing or pulling the stalk - high beam.
where: Rotary switch on the stalk or dashboard

when.s: Dusk is falling
when.d: Switch on low beam early so others can see you.

when.s: You want to flash a warning
when.d: Pull the stalk briefly; don't use it to bully drivers out of your way.

ctrl_headlamp.mistake: Driving at night on parking lights only.

ctrl_fog.more: Switches front (and sometimes rear) fog lamps. They're for fog and heavy rain only.
where: On the headlamp stalk or a separate button

when.s: Thick fog in the ghats at dawn
when.d: Switch fog lamps on with low beam and slow down.

when.s: The fog lifts
when.d: Switch them off so you don't dazzle others.

ctrl_fog.mistake: Driving with fog lamps on in clear weather for looks.

ctrl_clock.more: Central locking locks or unlocks every door at once; many cars also lock automatically above a set speed.
where: On the driver's door panel or the key fob
Many cars unlock automatically in a crash

when.s: You stop in an unfamiliar or crowded place
when.d: Keep the doors locked and windows up.

when.s: Passengers want to get out
when.d: Unlock only when stopped safely, and remind them to check for bikes first.

ctrl_clock.mistake: Leaving keys inside with the car on auto-lock.

ctrl_child.more: A small switch on the edge of each rear door. When set, the door can't be opened from inside.
where: On the edge of the rear doors (visible only when open)
Some cars have an electric child-lock button

when.s: Young children ride in the back
when.d: Set the child locks on both rear doors before the trip.

when.s: An adult passenger needs to get out
when.d: Open the door for them from outside.

ctrl_child.mistake: Forgetting to set them and a child opens the door while moving.

ctrl_window.more: Raises and lowers the window glass. Many cars have a lock button so rear passengers can't operate their windows.
where: Driver's door has a master panel and lock switch

when.s: Children are in the back
when.d: Use the window lock so they can't open windows or trap fingers.

when.s: You're closing a window with a child nearby
when.d: Watch until it's fully shut - some windows don't stop for fingers.

ctrl_window.mistake: Letting children stick their heads or hands out of the window.

ctrl_mirror.more: Adjusts the outside mirrors electrically. Set them so you see a sliver of your own car and as much of the next lane as possible.
where: A small joystick on the driver's door
Some cars also fold the mirrors with a button

when.s: You've just got into a car someone else drove
when.d: Adjust both mirrors before you move off.

when.s: You're parking in a narrow lane
when.d: Fold the mirrors in once parked.

ctrl_ignition.more: The key or Start/Stop button starts the engine. Push-button cars need the brake (or clutch) pressed to start.
where: Key slot on the steering column

when.s: The engine won't start on a push-button car
when.d: Press the brake firmly; if the key battery is weak, hold the key near the button.

when.s: You need to stop the engine in an emergency while moving
when.d: Most push-button cars stop the engine if you hold the button for a few seconds - steering stays, but becomes heavier.

ctrl_ignition.mistake: Turning the key to 'lock' while the car is still moving.

x2_notonga.more: Horse-drawn vehicles are kept off this road, usually because they are slow and horses can be startled by fast traffic. Other traffic is unaffected.

when.s: You are driving one of these: horse-drawn vehicles
when.d: Turn off before the sign and use the alternative route or service road.

when.s: You see one on the road anyway
when.d: Give it room and patience - it may be looking for a way off.

x2_notractor.more: Tractors are kept off this road, usually because they are slow, wide and may carry trailers that block lanes. Other traffic is unaffected.

when.s: You are driving one of these: tractors
when.d: Turn off before the sign and use the alternative route or service road.

when.s: You see one on the road anyway
when.d: Give it room and patience - it may be looking for a way off.

x2_nomoto.more: Scooters and motorcycles are kept off this road, usually because the road is fast, access-controlled, or a flyover where riders are at high risk. Other traffic is unaffected.

when.s: You are driving one of these: scooters and motorcycles
when.d: Turn off before the sign and use the alternative route or service road.

when.s: You see one on the road anyway
when.d: Give it room and patience - it may be looking for a way off.

x2_nobus.more: Buses are kept off this road, usually because the road is too narrow, has low structures, or buses have their own route. Other traffic is unaffected.
where: Old town lanes and low underpasses

when.s: You are driving one of these: buses
when.d: Turn off before the sign and use the alternative route or service road.

when.s: You see one on the road anyway
when.d: Give it room and patience - it may be looking for a way off.

x2_noauto.more: Auto-rickshaws are kept off this road, usually because the road is fast or access-controlled, or autos would stop and block traffic. Other traffic is unaffected.

when.s: You are driving one of these: auto-rickshaws
when.d: Turn off before the sign and use the alternative route or service road.

when.s: You see one on the road anyway
when.d: Give it room and patience - it may be looking for a way off.

x2_nocycrick.more: Cycle-rickshaws are kept off this road, usually because they are slow and unprotected on a fast road. Other traffic is unaffected.

when.s: You are driving one of these: cycle-rickshaws
when.d: Turn off before the sign and use the alternative route or service road.

when.s: You see one on the road anyway
when.d: Give it room and patience - it may be looking for a way off.

x2_minspeed.more: A blue circle with a number sets a minimum, used on fast roads where very slow vehicles would cause dangerous braking and lane changes behind them.
where: Fast lanes of some elevated roads

when.s: Your vehicle can't keep up, or a load makes you slow
when.d: Use another road, or the leftmost lane where one exists.

when.s: Traffic is jammed
when.d: You can drive slower than the minimum - it never forces you to be unsafe.

x2_minspeed.mistake: Crawling in the right lane on an expressway.

x2_endspeed.more: Ends the specific limit that was posted before. The general limits for that type of road and vehicle still apply.
where: Leaving a town or a school zone
After road works or a ghat section

when.s: You've left a 30 km/h school zone
when.d: Speed up gradually to a speed that suits the road and traffic.

when.s: Weather is poor
when.d: Stay slow - ending a limit doesn't make the road safer.

x2_endspeed.mistake: Accelerating hard the moment you pass the sign.

x2_endovertake.more: Marks where a no-overtaking stretch ends. Overtaking becomes allowed - not automatically safe.
where: After a ghat section or a series of bends
Past a narrow bridge or a school zone

when.s: You've been behind a slow lorry for kilometres
when.d: Wait for a long, clear straight with no junctions, then overtake decisively.

when.s: Oncoming traffic is close
when.d: Stay behind; the sign only removes the ban.

x2_endovertake.mistake: Pulling out the instant you see the sign without checking ahead.

x2_giveoncoming.more: On a single-lane stretch - narrow bridge, culvert or road works - traffic from the other side goes first. The opposite end usually has a 'priority over oncoming' sign.

when.s: An oncoming vehicle has entered the narrow part
when.d: Stop in the wider area before it and wait.

when.s: The narrow part is empty and you can see the far end
when.d: Go through steadily without stopping in the middle.

x2_giveoncoming.mistake: Racing an oncoming vehicle to the narrow section.

x2_passeither.more: Both sides of the island or obstruction are open in your direction - common on one-way roads and divided carriageways.
where: Toll plaza approaches and bridge piers

when.s: Vehicles are passing on both sides
when.d: Choose a side early and hold your line; don't switch at the last moment.

when.s: A two-wheeler is filtering on one side
when.d: Pass on the other side with room.

x2_passeither.mistake: Swerving from one side to the other just before the island.

x2_twoway.more: A one-way or divided road ends and traffic will soon come towards you in the same carriageway.
where: Where a four-lane highway narrows to two lanes
End of a one-way section in town

when.s: You're in the right-hand lane
when.d: Move left before the change; the right lane becomes the oncoming lane.

when.s: You were planning to overtake
when.d: Wait - you now share the road with oncoming traffic.

x2_twoway.mistake: Staying in the right lane out of habit after the divider ends.

x2_winding.more: A run of bends one after another - typical on ghat roads. The plate below may show the length of the winding stretch.
where: Ghat roads to Munnar, Wayanad, Ponmudi and Sabarimala
Roads through rubber and tea estates

when.s: A vehicle behind wants to pass
when.d: Keep left and let it pass on a straight where it can see; don't speed up.

when.s: Passengers feel car-sick
when.d: Drive smoothly with gentle steering and braking; stop at a safe wide spot if needed.

x2_winding.mistake: Cutting corners across the centre line.

x2_elephant.more: Wild elephants use this stretch to move between forest areas, often at dawn, dusk and night. A herd may include calves, and adults protect them aggressively.
where: Forest highways in Wayanad, Athirappilly, Aralam and Munnar
Roads near elephant corridors and reserves

when.s: Elephants are on or beside the road
when.d: Stop at a safe distance with the engine running, don't honk, flash lights or get out, and wait until they have crossed.

when.s: An elephant comes towards your vehicle
when.d: Reverse slowly away if the road behind is clear; never try to drive past it.

x2_elephant.mistake: Stopping close to take photos or videos.

x2_deer.more: Deer, wild boar, gaur and other animals cross here, especially at dawn and dusk. Where one animal crosses, others often follow.
where: Roads through wildlife sanctuaries and national parks
Forest edges and plantations at night

when.s: An animal crosses ahead
when.d: Slow down and wait - more may follow.

when.s: An animal freezes in your headlights
when.d: Dip your lights, slow or stop, and give it time to move.

x2_deer.mistake: Swerving violently to avoid a small animal and losing control.

x2_tunnel.more: A tunnel ahead. Your eyes need a few seconds to adjust to the dark when you enter and to the glare when you leave.
where: The Kuthiran tunnels near Thrissur, and other tunnels

when.s: You're entering the tunnel
when.d: Switch on headlights, remove sunglasses and slow down before the entrance.

when.s: Traffic stops inside the tunnel
when.d: Keep a good gap, switch on hazard lights and switch off the engine if you're stuck for long.

x2_tunnel.mistake: Overtaking or changing lanes inside the tunnel.

x2_flood.more: The road or causeway can go under water in heavy rain. Even shallow moving water can sweep a car away, and the road beneath may be washed out.
where: Low-lying roads in Kuttanad and near rivers
Causeways that are submerged in the monsoon

when.s: Water is flowing across the road
when.d: Turn back and find another route; don't try to drive through.

when.s: You've driven through standing water
when.d: Drive slowly afterwards and press the brakes lightly a few times to dry them.

x2_flood.mistake: Following a bus or lorry through deep water in a car.

x2_landslide.more: Saturated soil and rock can slide onto the road during and after heavy rain, sometimes taking part of the road with it.
where: Ghat roads in Idukki, Wayanad and Kozhikode
Hill highways after days of heavy rain

when.s: Mud, stones or cracks appear on the road
when.d: Slow down, don't stop under the slope, and turn back if the road looks undermined.

when.s: Authorities have closed the road or issued an alert
when.d: Don't travel on it; wait or take the advised route.

x2_landslide.mistake: Driving ghat roads at night during red-alert rain.

x2_rough.more: A broken surface, potholes or a row of humps. Hitting them fast can damage tyres and suspension and throw riders off balance.
where: Roads under repair and village roads after the monsoon
Rows of rumble humps before junctions

when.s: Potholes are full of water
when.d: Slow right down - you can't tell how deep they are.

when.s: You're on a two-wheeler
when.d: Hold the handlebar firmly, keep a steady line and don't brake hard on broken patches.

x2_rough.mistake: Swerving suddenly around each pothole into other traffic.

x2_lcmarker.more: Posts with three, two and one red bars count down your distance to a level crossing, so you can slow down in stages.
where: Approaches to railway level crossings on highways

when.s: You pass the three-bar post
when.d: Start slowing down and look for gate lights and bells.

when.s: You reach the one-bar post
when.d: You should be at a speed where you can stop easily before the crossing.

x2_lcmarker.mistake: Ignoring the markers and braking hard at the gate.

x2_subway.more: An underpass lets people cross a busy road safely without stepping into traffic.
where: Near railway stations and bus stands

when.s: You're walking and the subway is a little out of the way
when.d: Use it - the detour is short compared with the risk.

when.s: You're driving past the entrance
when.d: Don't stop or park near the stairs; people come out without looking.

x2_subway.mistake: Crossing on the road right above the subway.

x2_fob.more: A foot-over bridge carries pedestrians over a busy road or railway.
where: Over national highways near schools and markets

when.s: You're walking with heavy bags
when.d: Still use the bridge - vehicles on a highway can't stop in time.

when.s: You're driving under it
when.d: Watch for people who chose not to use it and cross below.

x2_fob.mistake: Climbing over the median below the bridge.

x2_toll.more: A toll plaza ahead. Lanes split into booths - FASTag lanes, cash lanes and lanes for oversized vehicles - and traffic slows suddenly.

when.s: You have FASTag
when.d: Choose a FASTag lane early and keep a gap; the barrier may not lift instantly.

when.s: The queue is long
when.d: Stay in your lane - weaving between booths causes many small crashes.

x2_toll.mistake: Changing lanes at the last moment inside the plaza.

x2_uturn.more: A place where turning round is allowed - usually a median gap or a dedicated U-turn bay.

when.s: You're in the U-turn bay
when.d: Wait for a real gap in the oncoming traffic; turn in one smooth movement.

when.s: Large vehicles are using the U-turn
when.d: Give them room - they may need several attempts.

x2_uturn.mistake: Starting the U-turn from the left lane across all the traffic.

x2_expy.more: From here the road is an expressway: fast, access-controlled and closed to slow vehicles, pedestrians, cycles and animals.

when.s: You join from the ramp
when.d: Use the acceleration lane to match the traffic speed, then merge into a gap.

when.s: You break down
when.d: Get onto the shoulder, switch on hazard lights, get everyone behind the barrier and call the helpline.

x2_expy.mistake: Stopping on the carriageway or reversing after missing an exit.

x2_expyend.more: The expressway ends. Ordinary roads have junctions, pedestrians, cycles, animals and slower vehicles again.
where: End of an expressway at a town
Where an access-controlled section rejoins the old highway

when.s: You've been driving fast for a long time
when.d: Check your speedometer - after long fast stretches, slower speeds feel like crawling.

when.s: A junction comes up soon after
when.d: Be ready to stop; signals and give-way rules apply again.

x2_expyend.mistake: Keeping expressway speed into the town.

x2_cng.more: A CNG filling station. CNG is stored at high pressure, so the rules on the forecourt are strict.

when.s: Your vehicle is being filled
when.d: Switch off the engine and get passengers out if the staff ask you to.

when.s: You decide to stop
when.d: Signal early, slow down in your lane and pull fully off the carriageway before stopping.

x2_cng.mistake: Joining a long queue that spills back onto the highway.

x2_ev.more: An electric-vehicle charging station. Charging can take anything from about half an hour to several hours.

when.s: Your car has finished charging
when.d: Move it so the next driver can charge.

when.s: You decide to stop
when.d: Signal early, slow down in your lane and pull fully off the carriageway before stopping.

x2_ev.mistake: Parking a petrol car in the charging bay.

when.s: Children or elderly passengers need a stop
when.d: Plan to stop here rather than on the roadside.

when.s: You decide to stop
when.d: Signal early, slow down in your lane and pull fully off the carriageway before stopping.

x2_toilet.mistake: Stopping on the carriageway near the sign.

x2_police.more: A police post or station is nearby - a safe place to report a crash, a theft or harassment.

when.s: You're being followed or feel unsafe
when.d: Drive to the police post and stop there.

when.s: You decide to stop
when.d: Signal early, slow down in your lane and pull fully off the carriageway before stopping.

x2_police.mistake: Leaving the scene of a crash instead of reporting it.

x2_airport.more: The road leads to an airport. Expect drop-off zones, security checks, slow-moving cabs and people with luggage.
where: Airport approach roads at Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Kozhikode and Kannur

when.s: You're dropping someone off
when.d: Use the departure kerb, unload quickly and move on; don't wait there.

when.s: You're picking someone up
when.d: Wait in the parking area until they're out, then drive to the pick-up point.

x2_airport.mistake: Stopping on the approach road to wait for a flight to land.

x2_rail.more: The road leads to a railway station. Around train times the area fills with autos, taxis and people crossing with luggage.

when.s: A train has just arrived
when.d: Drive slowly; people rush across the road to buses and autos.

when.s: You're dropping someone off
when.d: Use the drop-off area and don't block the entrance.

x2_helpline.more: Shows the highway helpline number. On national highways 1033 connects you to help for crashes and breakdowns; 112 is the all-emergency number.

when.s: You see a crash on the highway
when.d: Call 1033 or 112 with the road number and nearest kilometre stone.

when.s: Your vehicle breaks down on a fast road
when.d: Move to the shoulder, put on hazard lights, get people away from traffic, then call.

x2_helpline.mistake: Not noting the number and location before you need it.

x2_speedcam.more: Speed is measured by camera on this stretch, either at a point or as an average between two cameras.
where: Highways through towns and accident-prone stretches

when.s: You realise you're over the limit
when.d: Ease off smoothly - harsh braking can cause a rear-end crash.

when.s: Average-speed cameras are used
when.d: Keep to the limit for the whole stretch, not just at the camera.

x2_speedcam.mistake: Slamming the brakes at the camera and speeding again right after.

x2_buslane.more: A lane reserved for buses, so public transport isn't stuck in queues. A plate may give the hours.

when.s: You need to turn left from beyond the bus lane
when.d: Enter it only just before the turn, after checking for buses.

when.s: A bus is behind you in the bus lane
when.d: Move out of the lane as soon as it's safe.

x2_buslane.mistake: Using an empty bus lane to skip a queue.

x2_parkbus.more: Parking set aside for buses - tourist coaches, school and staff buses. Cars parked here force buses onto the road.

when.s: The bays are full
when.d: Don't double-park or block the entrance - find another legal spot.

when.s: You're leaving the bay
when.d: Check behind for pedestrians and other vehicles before you reverse out.

x2_parkbus.mistake: Using a bay meant for buses when you aren't one.

x2_ambulance.more: A bay kept free so ambulances can stop right at the door of a hospital or emergency point.
where: Large malls, stadiums and event venues

when.s: You're bringing a patient by car
when.d: Stop briefly to unload, then move to the car park.

when.s: The bay is empty and parking is full
when.d: Still keep out - an ambulance may arrive any moment.

x2_ambulance.mistake: Parking in the bay 'only for a few minutes'.

x3_dblYellow.more: Two continuous yellow lines down the middle, used where crossing into the other lane is especially dangerous.

when.s: You're stuck behind a slow lorry
when.d: Stay behind until the yellow lines end.

when.s: You need to turn right across the lines
when.d: Go on to a gap or junction where turning is allowed.

x3_dblYellow.mistake: Crossing the yellow lines to overtake on a bend.

x3_yelEdge.more: A yellow line along the kerb means no parking along that stretch; a sign may also ban stopping.

when.s: You need to drop someone off
when.d: Stop briefly only if stopping isn't also banned, and stay with the vehicle.

when.s: Everyone else is parked on it
when.d: Don't join them - find a legal spot.

x3_yelEdge.mistake: Parking along the yellow line 'only for a minute'.

x3_rumble.more: Raised bars that make the vehicle rumble and shake, waking you up to a hazard ahead - or warning that you're drifting off the road.
where: Before toll plazas, junctions and sharp bends

when.s: You feel the rumble before a junction
when.d: Slow down at once and look for what's ahead.

when.s: You hit edge rumble strips
when.d: You're drifting - steer back gently, and if you're tired, stop and rest.

x3_rumble.mistake: Driving on the rumble strips' edge to avoid the vibration.

x3_transBars.more: Lines across the lane that get closer together make you feel you're going faster, nudging you to slow down before a hazard.
where: Approaches to toll plazas and villages

when.s: The bars start passing quickly under you
when.d: Check your speedometer and ease off.

when.s: You're already slow
when.d: Keep a steady speed and look for the hazard ahead.

x3_chevron.more: A wedge of V-shaped stripes where a slip road splits off or joins. It keeps merging and diverging traffic apart.

when.s: You're about to miss your exit
when.d: Don't cut across the chevrons - take the next exit.

when.s: You're merging from a slip road
when.d: Merge at the end of the chevrons, not across them.

x3_chevron.mistake: Stopping on the chevrons to decide which way to go.

x3_busLane.more: BUS painted in a lane reserves it for buses; the colour or an extra sign may show the hours.

when.s: You need to turn left just ahead
when.d: Enter the bus lane only for the last short stretch, after checking for buses.

when.s: Traffic is jammed next to the empty bus lane
when.d: Stay out - it keeps buses on time for everyone.

x3_busLane.mistake: Stopping in the bus lane to drop passengers.

x3_island.more: A raised island with black-and-white kerbs divides traffic and gives pedestrians a place to wait.

when.s: The island has a keep-left sign
when.d: Pass on the left of it.

when.s: People are standing on the island
when.d: Slow down; they may step off in front of you.

x3_island.mistake: Clipping the island kerb at night by cutting the corner.

x3_refuge.more: A small island in the middle of a crossing so people can cross one direction of traffic at a time.

when.s: Someone is waiting on the refuge
when.d: Assume they'll step out; slow down and be ready to stop.

when.s: You're walking and reach the refuge
when.d: Stop there and check the second half of the road before going on.

x3_refuge.mistake: Overtaking near the refuge, where the road is narrowest.

x3_slowWord.more: SLOW painted on the road, stretched so it reads correctly from a moving vehicle.

when.s: You see SLOW and nothing obvious ahead
when.d: Slow down anyway - the hazard may be just out of sight.

when.s: It's raining
when.d: Slow down even more; painted words are slippery for two-wheelers.

x3_slowWord.mistake: Braking hard on the painted letters on a wet day.

x3_stopWord.more: STOP painted before a stop line reinforces a Stop sign at a dangerous junction.

when.s: You can see the road is empty
when.d: Still stop completely at the line, then look both ways.

when.s: The sign is missing but the word is painted
when.d: Treat it exactly like a Stop sign.

x3_studCol.more: Coloured reflective studs help you read the road at night. A common pattern is white between lanes, yellow along the median side and red at the left edge - but follow the painted lines where they differ.

when.s: Rain hides the paint
when.d: Use the stud colours to tell the lane line from the edge.

when.s: You cross a row of red studs
when.d: You're at the road edge - steer back.

x3_studCol.mistake: Mistaking the edge studs for a lane line.

x3_laneCombo.more: A lane arrow with a branch means traffic in that lane may go straight or turn the way the branch points.

when.s: You're going straight in a shared lane
when.d: Expect the vehicle ahead to stop and wait to turn.

when.s: You're turning from a shared lane
when.d: Signal clearly so drivers behind know you'll turn.

x3_laneCombo.mistake: Turning from a straight-only lane next to a shared one.

x3_cone.more: Orange cones with reflective bands guide traffic around works, crashes or checks, and close lanes temporarily.

when.s: Cones taper your lane away
when.d: Merge early and in turn - don't race to the last cone.

when.s: A cone has been knocked into your lane
when.d: Slow down and steer round it; don't run it over.

x3_cone.mistake: Moving cones aside to drive through a closed lane.

x3_barricade.more: Red-and-white striped boards close the road or part of it - for works, a hole, a collapse or an event.

when.s: The road ahead is barricaded
when.d: Stop and follow the diversion; never go round the barricade.

when.s: A barricade is placed partly across the lane
when.d: Slow down and pass only where the gap is clearly meant for traffic.

x3_barricade.mistake: Removing or squeezing past a barricade at night.

x3_diversion.more: A bold arrow board sends you off your usual route around a closure. Diversions are often narrow, unlit and busy.

when.s: The diversion goes through narrow lanes
when.d: Drive slowly and watch for pedestrians and parked vehicles.

when.s: You lose the diversion signs
when.d: Stop safely and check, rather than guessing into a one-way street.

x3_diversion.mistake: Ignoring the diversion and driving up to the closure.

x3_flagman.more: A worker with a STOP/SLOW paddle controls one-way flow through road works. Their signal must be obeyed like a traffic light.

when.s: STOP faces you
when.d: Stop behind the worker and wait, even if the road looks clear.

when.s: SLOW faces you
when.d: Drive through slowly, following the cones and any lead vehicle.

x3_flagman.mistake: Creeping forward or overtaking the queue while STOP is shown.

x3_delineator.more: Short reflective posts along the road edge trace the line of the road ahead, especially round bends and on embankments.

when.s: It's foggy or dark
when.d: Follow the posts to see where the road goes before your headlights reach the bend.

when.s: The posts curve sharply
when.d: Slow down early - the bend is tighter than the road suggests.

x3_delineator.mistake: Driving too fast for the visibility and relying only on the posts.

x3_convex.more: A round mirror at a blind bend or exit shows traffic you can't see directly. Mirrors make vehicles look smaller and further away than they are.
where: Exits from gates and car parks onto busy roads

when.s: You see a vehicle in the mirror
when.d: Assume it's closer and faster than it looks; wait or keep well left.

when.s: The mirror is empty
when.d: It may be dirty or have a blind area - still go slowly and sound the horn on hill bends.

x3_convex.mistake: Trusting the mirror completely and pulling out quickly.

x3_guardrail.more: A steel barrier along drops, bridges and sharp curves catches vehicles that leave the road. It marks the most dangerous edges.

when.s: You need to stop urgently on a guard-railed stretch
when.d: Pull as far left as safely possible, switch on hazards and get people behind the barrier.

when.s: You see a damaged section
when.d: Slow down - the protection there is gone.

x3_guardrail.mistake: Leaning or standing on the rail at a viewpoint near traffic.

x3_median.more: A raised, planted strip separating opposing traffic. Shrubs also cut glare from oncoming headlights.

when.s: Your turn is on the other side
when.d: Drive on to the next official gap or U-turn.

when.s: People cross through gaps in the plants
when.d: Watch for pedestrians stepping out of the median.

x3_median.mistake: Driving two-wheelers through a gap in the shrubs.

x3_plPrivate.more: Black characters on white mark a privately owned vehicle not used for hire. The first letters show the state (KL for Kerala) and the RTO code, followed by a series and number.
where: Personal vehicles registered in any state

when.s: You need to report a vehicle after a hit-and-run
when.d: Note the full number, colour and model - the state and RTO code come first.

when.s: Your own plate is dirty or cracked
when.d: Clean or replace it so it can be read by day and night.

x3_plPrivate.mistake: Using fancy fonts or stickers that make the number hard to read.

x3_plCommercial.more: Black on yellow marks a commercial vehicle - taxis, autos, buses and goods carriers used for hire or reward.

when.s: You're hiring a taxi
when.d: Check it has a yellow plate - it means it's registered for carrying passengers for hire.

when.s: A yellow-plate vehicle is ahead
when.d: Expect sudden stops to pick up or set down passengers or goods.

x3_plCommercial.mistake: Using a private car as a regular taxi.

x3_plRental.more: Yellow on black marks a self-drive rental vehicle - you hire the car and drive it yourself.

when.s: You're renting one
when.d: Check the papers, insurance and the car's condition, and photograph any damage before you leave.

when.s: You're driving an unfamiliar rental
when.d: Take a few minutes to find the lights, wipers and hazard switch before you set off.

x3_plRental.mistake: Driving a rental far harder than you would your own car.

x3_plEV.more: White on green marks a private electric vehicle. EVs are almost silent at low speed and accelerate quickly.

when.s: You're walking in a car park
when.d: Look as well as listen - an EV may be moving without a sound.

when.s: You're driving an EV near pedestrians
when.d: Go slowly and give extra room; they may not hear you.

x3_plEV.mistake: Assuming a silent vehicle isn't moving.

x3_plEVcomm.more: Yellow on green marks an electric vehicle used for hire - e-autos, e-buses and electric taxis.

when.s: An e-auto is ahead
when.d: Expect it to stop suddenly for passengers, like any auto.

when.s: You're crossing near a bus stop with e-buses
when.d: Look carefully - the bus may pull away almost silently.

x3_plEVcomm.mistake: Not hearing an e-bus and stepping out in front of it.

x3_plDiplo.more: White on blue with codes such as CD or CC marks vehicles of foreign missions and their staff.

when.s: You see one in traffic
when.d: Treat it like any other vehicle and drive normally.

when.s: It's part of an official convoy
when.d: Follow police instructions and give the convoy room.

x3_plDiplo.mistake: Trying to follow or photograph an official vehicle closely.

x3_plBH.more: The Bharat (BH) series starts with the year of registration, then BH, a number and letters. It's meant for people who move between states for work.
where: Vehicles of people in transferable jobs
Any state - the plate doesn't show a state code

when.s: You need to note a BH plate
when.d: Write it in order: year, BH, four digits, letters.

when.s: You're considering a BH registration
when.d: Check current eligibility rules with the RTO or Parivahan before applying.

x3_plBH.mistake: Assuming a BH-plate vehicle is from outside your state and 'not local'.

x3_plHSRP.more: A high-security plate has a chromium hologram of the Ashoka Chakra, IND in blue, a laser-etched number and non-reusable snap locks, making it hard to forge or swap.
where: Older vehicles that have been refitted

when.s: Your plate is damaged
when.d: Get a replacement through the authorised process, not a local copy.

when.s: You see a plate with HSRP features missing
when.d: It may be a fake - note other details if you need to report the vehicle.

x3_plHSRP.mistake: Replacing an HSRP with a decorative plate.

x3_learnerL.more: A red L on a white background, front and rear, shows the driver is a learner, who must be accompanied as the learner licence requires.

when.s: You're behind a learner who stalls at a signal
when.d: Be patient - don't hoot or overtake dangerously.

when.s: You're the learner
when.d: Display the L plates and practise first on quiet roads at quiet times.

x3_learnerL.mistake: Tailgating or cutting in front of learners to 'teach them'.

x3_reflTape.more: Red and white reflective tape outlines the back and sides of heavy vehicles so their size shows up in headlights.

when.s: You see tape low and wide ahead at night
when.d: It's likely a slow lorry or trailer - slow down early.

when.s: A trailer has no tape
when.d: Be extra careful; it may be almost invisible at night.

x3_reflTape.mistake: Misjudging the length of a trailer and cutting in too soon after overtaking.

x3_schoolBus.more: A yellow bus marked SCHOOL BUS (or 'On school duty') carries children. Children may get on and off at any roadside stop.
where: Mornings and afternoons on school days

when.s: The bus stops with children getting off
when.d: Slow right down or stop - a child may run round the front of the bus.

when.s: You're behind it on a narrow road
when.d: Keep a good distance; it stops often.

x3_schoolBus.mistake: Overtaking a stopped school bus at speed.

x3_ambulance.more: An ambulance with lights and siren is carrying a patient or racing to one. Minutes matter.

when.s: You hear a siren but can't see where it is
when.d: Slow down, check mirrors and look around before moving over.

when.s: You're at a red light and it's behind you
when.d: Move over only if you can do so safely; don't drive into the junction dangerously.

x3_ambulance.mistake: Following an ambulance closely to get through traffic.

x3_fireEngine.more: A red fire tender with beacons and siren on its way to a fire or rescue. It's heavy and needs space to manoeuvre.

when.s: A fire engine approaches
when.d: Pull left and stop where safe; let it pass and watch for a second one.

when.s: You park near a hydrant or fire station gate
when.d: Don't - keep those spaces clear at all times.

x3_fireEngine.mistake: Parking across the fire station exit.

x3_laneCtl.more: Signals above each lane open or close it - common on tunnels, toll plazas, bridges and tidal-flow roads.

when.s: A red cross appears over your lane
when.d: Move to a lane with a green arrow as soon as it's safe.

when.s: An amber diagonal arrow appears
when.d: Change lanes in the direction shown - your lane is closing ahead.

x3_laneCtl.mistake: Staying in a red-cross lane because it's empty.

x3_levelX.more: Alternately flashing red lights at a level crossing mean a train is coming. Barriers may follow.

when.s: The lights start flashing as you approach
when.d: Stop behind the line, even if the barrier is still up.

when.s: A train has passed but the lights keep flashing
when.d: Wait - another train may be coming.

x3_schoolFlash.more: A flashing amber light on a school sign shows that the school zone is active - children are arriving or leaving.

when.s: The light is flashing
when.d: Drive at a crawl, be ready to stop and watch between parked vehicles.

when.s: A traffic warden is crossing children
when.d: Stop and wait for the warden's signal.

x3_schoolFlash.mistake: Assuming the light is just decoration outside school hours.

x3_pedPush.more: A push button lets pedestrians call a green walking phase at a crossing that otherwise stays green for vehicles.

when.s: You're walking
when.d: Press once and wait for the green figure - pressing again doesn't speed it up.

when.s: You're driving and the light turns amber
when.d: Someone has pressed the button; stop for the crossing.

x3_pedPush.mistake: Crossing before the signal changes because the button 'takes too long'.

x3_countRed.more: A countdown under the red light tells you how long you'll wait - useful for deciding to switch off the engine.
where: Long signal cycles at city junctions

when.s: The countdown shows a long wait
when.d: Switch off the engine if it's more than about a minute.

when.s: It reaches zero
when.d: Wait for the green light itself, then check the junction is clear before moving.

x3_countRed.mistake: Starting to roll as the numbers count down.
